title: XCancel and Nitter Receive Cease and Desist Letters from XCorp
summary: XCorp (formerly Twitter) has issued cease and desist letters to the developers of XCancel and Nitter, two open-source projects that provided alternative frontends to X/Twitter. Both services have temporarily shut down while seeking legal advice. XCancel and Nitter allowed users to access X/Twitter content without logging in or encountering ads, but their operations have now been halted due to legal pressure.
key_points: XCorp sent cease and desist letters to XCancel and Nitter, demanding permanent takedowns.
XCancel and Nitter were open-source alternatives to X/Twitter, allowing ad-free and login-free access.
Both services have temporarily ceased operations while developers seek legal counsel.
Users relied on these tools to bypass X/Twitter's restrictive login requirements and ads.
The shutdown highlights XCorp's shift toward a more closed, ad-driven platform model.
The incident underscores challenges faced by open-source projects when dealing with corporate legal actions.
